elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, etc.)
sub_elements.evidence: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ (project URL); a publication DOI (10.1007/s12028-024-02007) and grant OT2OD032701 appear but no dataset-level DOI/RRID
sub_elements.quality_note: No persistent dataset identifier; the id is the project landing URL, and the only DOI is for an associated publication, not the dataset itself

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI; description spans ~1000 chars covering scope, modalities, standards, and current counts
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear title plus comprehensive description with concrete scope (20 centers, 100K+ target, multi-modal data, OMOP standardization)

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [CHoRUS, Bridge2AI, critical care, OMOP Common Data Model, EHR, waveform telemetry, DICOM, EEG, health equity, ...] (26 terms)
sub_elements.quality_note: 26 relevant keywords spanning domain, modalities, standards, and methods

sub_elements.name: Dataset Landing Page or Platform URL
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://chorus4ai.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: Active project landing page provided

sub_elements.name: Associated Project or Program
sub_elements.evidence: description: 'CHoRUS for Equitable AI is a Bridge2AI data generation project'; external_resources include Bridge2AI program links
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear association with the NIH Bridge2AI program

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Mechanism Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'Dataset distributed under controlled access requiring institutional email registration and signed licensing agreement. Access granted after review and approval process.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Controlled/registered access clearly stated with review-and-approval workflow

sub_elements.name: Data Use Agreement Required?
sub_elements.evidence: license_terms: 'All participants must sign a licensing agreement before gaining access'; 'Institutional (.edu) email required for registration'; access contacts dbold@emory.edu / jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org
sub_elements.quality_note: DUA explicitly required with registration steps and named access-request contacts

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats access_urls: https://chorus4ai.org/; 'users receive email with access instructions to CHoRUS secure enclave (Azure-based infrastructure)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform access route and enclave instructions provided, though controlled access means no direct download link

sub_elements.name: File Formats Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: OMOP CDM, WFDB, DICOM, OHNLP tokenized, EDF+/Persyst
sub_elements.quality_note: Five specific formats enumerated per modality

sub_elements.name: External Links to Similar or Related Datasets
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: Bridge2AI program, OHDSI/OMOP community, AIM-AHEAD, NIH RePORTER, GitHub org, Neurocritical Care publication
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple related resources and repositories linked

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.evidence: license_terms: 'Data use agreement specifies permitted research uses and prohibits re-identification'; GitHub tooling under MIT/Apache-2.0 licenses
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse permissions (research use) and constraints clearly specified; associated code licenses named

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model, WFDB (PhysioNet), DICOM, EDF+, OHNLP schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Uses widely adopted standard formats across all modalities

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: cleaning_strategies: 'validated against published metadata schemas (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, OHNLP, EDF+, Persyst)'; OMOP CDM transformation with OMOP vocabulary standards
sub_elements.quality_note: Explicit conformance to OMOP CDM and multiple published metadata schemas documented

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Defined for Linking
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit statement of participant/admission identifiers or linking keys across modalities
sub_elements.quality_note: OMOP structure implies person/admission IDs but no linking keys or identifier fields are described for joining across the modalities

sub_elements.name: Documentation of Processing Tools for Reproducibility
sub_elements.evidence: chorus_waveform, chorus-mapping, privacy_scan_tool, UF-Geocoding (DeGauss), CHoRUSReports, chorus-extract-upload across github.com/chorus-ai (28 repositories)
sub_elements.quality_note: Named open-source tools and repositories for extraction, mapping, and QC

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review Documented
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research ethics_review_board: 'Institutional review boards at 14 data acquisition centers'; 'Community-facing ethics focus groups'
sub_elements.quality_note: IRB oversight at all contributing sites plus community ethics focus groups documented

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.evidence: preproc:4 DICOM header de-identification; preproc:2 OHNLP tokenization; preproc:5 're-identification limitation transformations'; privacy_scan_tool for privacy scanning
sub_elements.quality_note: Modality-specific de-identification methods described, though not tied to a named regulatory standard (e.g., HIPAA Safe Harbor/Expert Determination)

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Removed or Masked
sub_elements.evidence: sensitivity_details: 'Demographics and patient identifiers (de-identified before controlled access release)'; 'DICOM metadata (de-identification in process)'; 'Embedded patient information being removed'
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific identifier categories and their removal/masking status enumerated per modality

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research describes retrospective collection approved via IRB and legal framework, but no consent procedure or consent type is stated
sub_elements.quality_note: Retrospective collection is described but informed consent (type/procedure/waiver) is not documented

sub_elements.name: Ethical Sourcing Statement Included
sub_elements.evidence: description: 'ethically sourced'; gap:3 patient-focused efforts to manage privacy and bias; 'community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear ethical-sourcing position with community engagement and SDOH-aware framing

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure

strengths: Exceptional funding transparency with full grant identifiers (OT2OD032701 / 1OT2OD032701-01), opportunity number, study section, and funding amount
Detailed, modality-specific technical transparency: collection devices, preprocessing pipelines, cleaning strategies, and named open-source repositories across the chorus-ai GitHub organization
Comprehensive data composition with concrete counts (45K+ admissions, 50K released, 1.6B OMOP rows, 23 TB waveform) across five clearly enumerated modalities
Strong interoperability via standardization to OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB/PhysioNet, OHNLP, and EDF+/Persyst schemas
Robust ethical framing with multi-site IRB oversight, community ethics focus groups, and modality-specific de-identification methods
weaknesses: No provenance/version tracking: missing dataset version number, release notes, and per-version change descriptions (Element 6 scored 1/5)
No persistent dataset identifier (DOI/RRID); the id field is the project landing URL and the only DOI is for an associated publication
Informed-consent procedures for the retrospective cohort are not documented
Cross-modality linking identifiers are not explicitly described, and the dataset is hosted on a custom enclave rather than a recognized public repository
recommendations: Mint and record a persistent dataset DOI (e.g., via DataCite/Zenodo) distinct from the associated publication DOI
Add a dataset_version field with release_notes documenting versioned change history as the cohort expands from 45K toward 100K+ admissions
Document the informed-consent basis (consent type, IRB waiver of consent, or authorization) for the retrospective critical-care cohort
Add a conflicts-of-interest statement covering the consortium investigators
State the participant/admission linking keys used across modalities (e.g., OMOP person_id / visit_occurrence_id) to support cross-modal integration and reuse
